# Remove-ZbxItem

## SYNOPSIS

Removes items.

## SYNTAX

```
Remove-ZbxItem [-InputObject] <ZabbixReference<ZabbixItem>[]> [-Force] [-Connection <ZabbixConnection>] [-WhatIf] [-Confirm] [<CommonParameters>]
```

## DESCRIPTION

An item collects one kind of value from a host, such as CPU load, free disk space or a log line, on a schedule or as values are sent to it. The Remove-ZbxItem cmdlet deletes the items given to -InputObject (names, ids or piped objects) with item.delete, all in one call when the pipeline ends. It asks for confirmation first unless -Confirm:$false or -Force is given, and -WhatIf lists what would be deleted. It writes nothing, and needs a connection made with Connect-ZbxServer.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1: Delete an item

```powershell
$item = Get-ZbxItem -Host 'web-01' -Name 'Queue length'
Remove-ZbxItem -InputObject $item -Confirm:$false
```

-InputObject takes an id, an item object or a name (a name must be unique on the server, so pass the object when several hosts have an item of that name). ConfirmImpact is High: -Confirm:$false skips the prompt.

### Example 2: Delete the items a search finds, through the pipeline

```powershell
Get-ZbxItem -Host 'web-01' -Search @{ key_ = 'app.queue' } | Remove-ZbxItem -WhatIf
Get-ZbxItem -Host 'web-01' -Search @{ key_ = 'app.queue' } | Remove-ZbxItem -Confirm:$false
Get-ZbxItem -Host 'web-01' | Select-Object Name, Key
```

Get-ZbxItem writes item objects; Remove-ZbxItem binds each one. -WhatIf lists what would be deleted.

## PARAMETERS

### -InputObject

The item(s) to change or delete: ids, names or objects, from the pipeline or by position. -Id is an alias.

## INPUTS

- `ZabbixReference<ZabbixItem>[]`: Bound to -InputObject (ByValue). Represents a reference to an API object: a parameter that points at an API object takes its id, its name, or the object itself piped from a Get- cmdlet, and becomes an id before the call — one parameter, three spellings, one resolution.
